- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at +3–4 points above peak for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct — apply slight upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings — dampen forecast volatility if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +1.00), model often misaligns with true trend — use weighted average of recent 5–7 days for smoothing.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), model often overfits to recent highs — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5 points to avoid overconfidence.
